To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectral decomposition of CFP is a powerful tool to study the relationship between CFP and brain morphology, in particular the relationship between brain size and the number of folds and their complexity.

the frequency spectrum of curvature is a relevant descriptor of the folding pattern of the human cortex and that larger brains have more complex folding pattern because of an increase of high spatial frequency elements.
cortical folding pattern can be segmented based on its spectral composition, that this segmentation reveals 3 orders of folds, and that the number of 3rd order folds increase with brain size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description and quantification of CFP.
the description of cortical folding patterns and its relationship to brain size.
the description of CFP in a geometric framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the folding pattern of the adult human brain is characterized by a constant contribution of 1st and 2nd order elements, an increasing contribution of 3rd order, and an increasing contribution of the highest spatial frequency elements.
the spectral analysis of CFP provides a powerful and relevant method to study the relationship between brain size and CFP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the folding pattern is a complex, hierarchical, multi-scale structure that is organized in frequency bands and that its complexity increases allometrically.
the spectral composition of cortical folding pattern is a good proxy of brain size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectral analysis of CFP provides a powerful and flexible framework for describing cortical folding pattern and for investigating the mechanisms underlying its evolution.
a spectral analysis of curvature can reveal the hierarchical organization of CFP and provide a quantitative description of the relationship between brain size, folding power and complexity.
a Fourier-like analysis applied on a cortical surface mesh provides a powerful tool to describe and analyze CFP, which is particularly useful to study the relationship between brain size and folding.
